raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
Removing MRV1 (#63373) from under MRV2 DBO is two PRs:

-> #64668 [1/2][MRV2] Remove the dependency of MRV2 DBO from MRV1
   #64718 [2/2][MRV2] Abort sibling microbatches when one fails

## Overview

Make MRV2 DBO independent of MRV1. MRV2 DBO no longer references anything that #63373 (Remove MRV1) deletes. The DBO helpers that both runners share move unchanged into one runner-agnostic MRV2 module, so a future runner can reuse them as-is.

## Claims

- **No MRV1 code in MRV2 DBO.** `create_ubatch_slices` computes the padded slices itself instead of calling V1's `maybe_create_ubatch_slices` and then clamping the result. Output is unchanged.
- **Shared helpers have one home.** `UBatchSlice`/`UBatchSlices`, the SM control context, `get_num_ubatches` and `check_ubatch_thresholds` move verbatim to `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/ubatch_common.py`, along with the slice computation (`compute_ubatch_slices`). MRV2 and `forward_context` import them from there. `vllm/v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py` re-exports them for the V1 runner, so each symbol still has exactly one definition and V1 code is untouched.
- **Tests no longer depend on V1.** The MRV2 slicing tests pin the same five layouts to explicit values instead of using V1's `split_attn_metadata` as an oracle. The integer-bounds check in `test_ubatch_offsets.py` now covers the shared `compute_ubatch_slices`, with padding. The V1 `UBatchWrapper` test moves unchanged to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py`, so MRV1 removal can delete it on its own. Only the V1 runner and the V1 test `test_attention_splitting.py` still call V1's `maybe_create_ubatch_slices`.

## Validation

Base: main `1fbde73aa1`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CPU: `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py`, `test_gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py`, `test_ubatch_offsets.py` | 30 passed, 10 hardware skips (same as main) |
| CPU: `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py` (V1, uses the re-exported names) | 23 passed |
| Equivalence: new slicing vs. old V1 call plus clamp, 187,261 random cases (2–4 microbatches, request/token padding, uniform spec-decode splits, int32/int64 counts) | identical; every bound is a Python `int` |
| Mutation: request start off by one | 13 tests fail |
| Moved code | AST-identical to the original for all six definitions; each is defined once in `vllm/` |
| Imports, each in a fresh process: `forward_context`, V1 `ubatch_utils`/`dp_utils`/`gpu_model_runner`/`gpu_ubatch_wrapper`, MRV2 `model_runner`/`ubatch_utils`, elastic EP | all OK; importing `ubatch_common` loads no other MRV2 module and no `forward_context` |
| Cross-check against #63373 (`cfd92bd0f0`): its 35 deleted `.py` files and 49 deleted functions/classes, searched in MRV2 DBO code and tests | 0 references |
| **Simulated merge with #63373**: its diff applied file by file onto this head (38 deletions incl. `gpu_model_runner.py`, `gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py`, `gpu_input_batch.py`; 96 modifications; 12 non-DBO files hand-skipped for main drift, 2 hand-resolved) | `ubatch_common`, V1 `ubatch_utils`, `ubatching`, `forward_context`, MRV2 `ubatch_utils`/`dp_utils`/`cudagraph_utils`/`model_runner`, `gpu_worker`, elastic EP and `modular_kernel` all import; MRV2 DBO tests 28 passed, 10 hardware skips (the 2 V1 wrapper cases are deleted with MRV1) |
| `ruff check`/`format`, SPDX, forbidden imports, `torch.cuda` call, lazy imports, test tethering, boolean context manager | pass |
| mypy (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11`) on all changed files plus their V1 importers | 72 errors before and after, identical; none in the new module |

```bash
VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py -q
```

### GPU

Head `a80aa532e2` against its base, main `1fbde73aa1`, on H200 (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129). `_C_stable_libtorch` and `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` were built from `1fbde73aa1`. This PR does not touch `csrc`, so both trees load the same binaries.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| GPU: the same four test files, 1x H200 | 63 passed, 0 skipped (the 10 CPU hardware skips run) |
| Serving: DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16, DP2/TP1/EP2, NIXL EP, `--enable-dbo` (decode/prefill thresholds 8/64), FULL graphs (capture 16/32/64/128) | Base and head start and serve. Every step splits into two non-empty microbatches on both ranks (155 splits per rank in each run) |
| Same, `--enforce-eager` | Same; 144–146 splits per rank |
| Greedy tokens, 144 requests per run (96 mixed prefill/decode, then 48 decode-heavy; `ignore_eos`), base once, head twice | FULL: base vs head 2 differ, head vs head 1. Eager: base vs head 19, head vs head 18 (median first divergent token 22 vs 21.5) |

Two runs of the same head differ at the same rate and depth as base vs head. Per-step batch composition also differs between the two head runs, so greedy MoE/EP output is not bit-reproducible here. The serving runs show no PR-attributable difference. Exact slice equivalence rests on the 187,261-case check above.

Not run: performance, DeepEP backends, multi-node, and the simulated #63373 merge on GPU.

## Details

**Why move instead of copy:** two copies of `UBatchSlice` would be distinct types, and mypy would reject MRV2 passing its slices into `forward_context`. The SM control code also still receives backend fixes (for example `comm_sms=0` for ROCm DeepEP HT), and a copy would drift.

**Why the module lives in `gpu/` but stays runner-agnostic:** it imports only config, platform and utility modules. `forward_context` and the V1 runner can import it without a cycle, and a later runner can import it directly or take the file as-is.

**Deliberately unchanged:**
- `vllm/v1/worker/ubatching.py` — the `dbo_*` handoff protocol that MoE prepare/finalize, model layers and the workspace call. It holds process-global state, so it must stay a single module, and #63373 keeps it.
- `skip_dp_coordination` in `vllm/v1/worker/dp_utils.py` — a `ContextVar` that elastic EP sets. A copy would be a separate flag that MRV2 never sees set. It is DP coordination, not DBO.
- `maybe_create_ubatch_slices`, `_pad_out_ubatch_slices`, `is_last_ubatch_empty` and `split_attn_metadata` — after this PR only V1 uses them, so they go away with MRV1.

**Interaction with #63373:** both PRs edit the top import block of `vllm/v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py`, so they conflict textually there. #63373 drops the `CommonAttentionMetadata` import, and this PR replaces the block with the re-export. The resolution is to keep the re-export and drop that import together with the three functions #63373 deletes; the simulation above used exactly this. #63373's `test_attention_splitting.py` still imports the functions it deletes; that V1 test needs updating or deleting there, independently of this PR.

**Config gate (unchanged here):** on main, a DBO config with a feature MRV2 lacks (`_get_dbo_unsupported_features`: LoRA, hybrid, PP, CP, pure PIECEWISE, …) silently falls back to MRV1. At #63373's head the same check raises `ValueError`. This PR changes neither behavior.

**Not a duplicate:** open-PR searches for `ubatch_utils` and "model runner V1 DBO" found nothing similar. #63373 removes MRV1 itself and leaves this call, the test oracle and the shared block in place.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Dual batch overlap (DBO) in the V1 model runner's `UBatchWrapper`."""
+
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.v1.worker import gpu_ubatch_wrapper as legacy_gpu_ubatch_wrapper
+from vllm.v1.worker.ubatch_utils import UBatchSlice
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("cudagraph_runtime_mode", "execution_method"),
+    [
+        (CUDAGraphMode.FULL, "_capture_ubatches"),
+        (CUDAGraphMode.NONE, "_run_ubatches"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_legacy_ubatch_contexts_slice_padding_mask(
+    cudagraph_runtime_mode: CUDAGraphMode, execution_method: str
+):
+    """Replacement contexts preserve each microbatch's padding rows."""
+    ubatch_slices = [
+        UBatchSlice(slice(0, 2), slice(0, 3)),
+        UBatchSlice(slice(2, 4), slice(3, 6)),
+    ]
+    is_padding = torch.tensor([False, True, False, True, False, True])
+    forward_context = SimpleNamespace(
+        batch_descriptor=object(),
+        ubatch_slices=ubatch_slices,
+        cudagraph_runtime_mode=cudagraph_runtime_mode,
+        attn_metadata=[{}, {}],
+        slot_mapping={},
+        dp_metadata=object(),
+        is_padding=is_padding,
+    )
+
+    wrapper = object.__new__(legacy_gpu_ubatch_wrapper.UBatchWrapper)
+    wrapper.vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(data_parallel_size=2)
+    )
+    wrapper.comm_stream = object()
+    wrapper.ready_barrier = object()
+    wrapper.cudagraphs = {}
+    wrapper.sm_control = nullcontext()
+    wrapper.runnable = object()
+
+    def make_contexts(*, forward_contexts, **kwargs):
+        return [
+            SimpleNamespace(id=i, forward_context=context)
+            for i, context in enumerate(forward_contexts)
+        ]
+
+    def create_context(attn_metadata, vllm_config, **kwargs):
+        return SimpleNamespace(attn_metadata=attn_metadata, **kwargs)
+
+    model_inputs = {
+        "input_ids": torch.arange(6),
+        "positions": torch.arange(6),
+        "inputs_embeds": None,
+        "intermediate_tensors": None,
+    }
+    expected = object()
+    with (
+        patch.object(
+            legacy_gpu_ubatch_wrapper,
+            "get_forward_context",
+            return_value=forward_context,
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            legacy_gpu_ubatch_wrapper.torch.cuda,
+            "current_stream",
+            return_value=object(),
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            legacy_gpu_ubatch_wrapper.DPMetadata, "make", return_value=object()
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            legacy_gpu_ubatch_wrapper,
+            "create_forward_context",
+            side_effect=create_context,
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            legacy_gpu_ubatch_wrapper,
+            "make_ubatch_contexts",
+            side_effect=make_contexts,
+        ),
+        patch.object(wrapper, execution_method, return_value=expected) as execute,
+    ):
+        result = wrapper(**model_inputs)
+
+    assert result is expected
+    contexts = [
+        metadata.context.forward_context for metadata in execute.call_args.args[0]
+    ]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(contexts[0].is_padding, is_padding[:3])
+    torch.testing.assert_close(contexts[1].is_padding, is_padding[3:])

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Runner-agnostic microbatching (DBO) helpers.
+
+This module must not import `vllm.forward_context` or other model runner
+modules: `forward_context` and the V1 model runner import it.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TypeAlias
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.config import ParallelConfig
+from vllm.distributed import get_ep_group
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import set_num_sms as deep_gemm_set_num_sms
+from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_deep_gemm
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import num_compute_units
+
+
+@dataclass
+class UBatchSlice:
+    request_slice: slice
+    token_slice: slice
+
+    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
+        return (
+            self.request_slice.start == self.request_slice.stop
+            or self.token_slice.start == self.token_slice.stop
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def num_tokens(self) -> int:
+        return self.token_slice.stop - self.token_slice.start
+
+
+UBatchSlices: TypeAlias = list[UBatchSlice]
+
+
+class SMControlContextManager:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        comm_sms: int,
+        set_comm_sms: Callable[[int], None],
+        set_compute_sms: Callable[[int], None],
+    ):
+        """Context manager for controlling SM (Streaming Multiprocessor)
+        allocation. Upon entering the context, it sets the number of SMs
+        allocated for communication and computation to comm_sms and
+        total_sms - comm_sms respectively. Upon exiting, it restores the
+        allocation to use all available SMs (i.e. total_sms).
+
+        Args:
+            comm_sms (int): The number of SMs to allocate for communication.
+                (The remainder will be used for computation.)
+            set_comm_sms (Callable[[int], None]):
+                A function that sets the number of SMs for communication.
+            set_compute_sms (Callable[[int], None]):
+                A function that sets the number of SMs for computation.
+
+        """
+        assert current_platform.is_cuda() or current_platform.is_rocm(), (
+            "SM/CU control is supported on CUDA and ROCm platforms"
+        )
+        device = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+        total_sms = num_compute_units(device)
+
+        assert comm_sms < total_sms
+        self.total_sms = total_sms
+        self.compute_sms = total_sms - comm_sms
+        self.comm_sms = comm_sms
+        self.set_comm_sms = set_comm_sms
+        self.set_compute_sms = set_compute_sms
+
+    def __enter__(self):
+        self.set_comm_sms(self.comm_sms)
+        self.set_compute_sms(self.compute_sms)
+
+    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
+        self.set_comm_sms(self.total_sms)
+        self.set_compute_sms(self.total_sms)
+
+
+def create_sm_control_context(
+    parallel_config: ParallelConfig,
+) -> SMControlContextManager:
+    """Reserve SMs for communication kernels while microbatches overlap."""
+    comm_sms: int = envs.VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS
+    rocm_deepep_ht_dbo = (
+        current_platform.is_rocm()
+        and parallel_config.enable_dbo
+        and parallel_config.all2all_backend == "deepep_high_throughput"
+    )
+    if rocm_deepep_ht_dbo:
+        # On ROCm, reserving CUs for DeepEP HT communication under DBO
+        # corrupts DP+EP generation accuracy. Keep the backend active, but
+        # leave all CUs visible to the compute and communication kernels.
+        comm_sms = 0
+
+    set_comm_sms = lambda sms: None
+    if parallel_config.enable_expert_parallel:
+        # Currently only DeepEP highthroughput supports SM control so this
+        # only affects that case.
+        ep_group = get_ep_group()
+        device_communicator = ep_group.device_communicator
+        all2all_manager = None
+        if device_communicator is not None:
+            all2all_manager = device_communicator.all2all_manager
+
+        if all2all_manager is not None:
+            max_sms_used = all2all_manager.max_sms_used()
+            if max_sms_used is not None:
+                comm_sms = min(comm_sms, max_sms_used)
+
+        if comm_sms > 0 and all2all_manager is not None:
+            set_comm_sms = lambda sms: all2all_manager.set_num_sms(sms)
+
+    # TODO(lucas): support other kernels besides DeepGEMM
+    set_compute_sms = lambda sms: None
+    if has_deep_gemm() and comm_sms > 0:
+        set_compute_sms = lambda sms: deep_gemm_set_num_sms(sms)
+
+    return SMControlContextManager(
+        comm_sms=comm_sms,
+        set_comm_sms=set_comm_sms,
+        set_compute_sms=set_compute_sms,
+    )
+
+
+def get_num_ubatches(parallel_config: ParallelConfig) -> int:
+    """How many microbatches a step is split into; 1 when microbatching is off."""
+    return parallel_config.num_ubatches if parallel_config.use_ubatching else 1
+
+
+def check_ubatch_thresholds(
+    config: ParallelConfig, num_tokens: int, uniform_decode: bool
+) -> bool:
+    if not config.use_ubatching:
+        return False
+    if uniform_decode:
+        return num_tokens >= config.dbo_decode_token_threshold
+    else:
+        return num_tokens >= config.dbo_prefill_token_threshold
+
+
+def compute_ubatch_slices(
+    num_scheduled_tokens: np.ndarray,
+    num_reqs: int,
+    num_reqs_padded: int,
+    num_tokens_padded: int,
+    num_ubatches: int,
+    uniform_token_count: int | None = None,
+) -> UBatchSlices:
+    """Split a DP-padded batch into the slices its microbatches run on.
+
+    Splitting at the midpoint of the DP-padded token count leaves the trailing
+    microbatch anywhere from full to entirely inside the padding. Clamping its
+    request slice onto the last request leaves it holding that request with
+    zero query tokens -- the shape a straddling request already takes -- so it
+    stays well-formed with no work to do, like a dummy run.
+
+    A uniform batch of multi-token queries (spec decode verification) is split
+    on a request boundary instead, so each microbatch stays a uniform decode.
+    `uniform_token_count` must be agreed across DP ranks.
+    """
+    split_point = num_tokens_padded // num_ubatches
+    if uniform_token_count is not None and uniform_token_count > 1:
+        reqs_per_ubatch = num_tokens_padded // (uniform_token_count * num_ubatches)
+        if reqs_per_ubatch > 0:
+            split_point = reqs_per_ubatch * uniform_token_count
+    token_bounds = [split_point * i for i in range(num_ubatches)]
+    token_bounds.append(num_tokens_padded)
+
+    cu_num_tokens = np.zeros(len(num_scheduled_tokens) + 1, np.int32)
+    np.cumsum(num_scheduled_tokens, out=cu_num_tokens[1:])
+
+    ubatch_slices = []
+    for i in range(num_ubatches):
+        start, stop = token_bounds[i], token_bounds[i + 1]
+        # The microbatch holds the requests overlapping [start, stop); the
+        # trailing one also takes every padded request.
+        req_start = int(np.searchsorted(cu_num_tokens, start, side="right")) - 1
+        req_stop = num_reqs_padded
+        if i < num_ubatches - 1:
+            req_stop = int(np.searchsorted(cu_num_tokens, stop, side="left"))
+        ubatch_slices.append(
+            UBatchSlice(
+                slice(min(req_start, num_reqs - 1), min(req_stop, num_reqs_padded)),
+                slice(start, stop),
+            )
+        )
+    return ubatch_slices
